drawings.description: un graphe des types d'ateliers, reliés par des traits et des flèches. En haut, « Atelier général $(\mathcal{A};\trianglelefteq,\mathring{\ll},|o|)$ » cerclé ($\mathcal{A}$) ; sous lui « Atelier divisible » (souligné, traversé par le trait qui monte vers l'atelier général). Au niveau suivant : « atelier spatial $(\mathcal{A};\trianglelefteq,|o|)$ » avec $\Sigma$ cerclé, relié à l'atelier général ; « atelier local $(\mathcal{A};\trianglelefteq,\mathring{\ll},|o|_{\mathcal{L}})$ » ; « atelier fidèle $(\mathcal{A};\trianglelefteq,\mathring{\ll})$ », relié à l'atelier général. Plus bas, « atelier ponctuel $\Sigma\simeq\mathfrak{P}(\mathcal{L})$ », relié à l'atelier local et à l'atelier fidèle, et par un trait tireté à l'atelier spatial ; une flèche de l'atelier spatial et une flèche de l'atelier ponctuel descendent vers ($\mathcal{L}$) « atelier ensembliste », d'où une flèche vers « at. ens. modéré », puis vers « at. discret », puis vers « at.-point » (au-dessus, un mot biffé, \ill{}). À droite, « atelier modéré » (un premier « atelier modéré » est biffé plus haut) reçoit une longue courbe venue de l'atelier général et une autre de l'atelier fidèle, avec au crayon « at. mod ? » ; une flèche tiretée en part vers « at. ens. modéré » ; « maquette $\Sigma\simeq\mathfrak{P}(\mathcal{A})$ », encadrée au crayon, est reliée par une double flèche à l'atelier modéré et envoie une flèche vers « at. discret ». Un trait horizontal orangé sépare « at. discret » et « at.-point » du reste.
drawings.kind: graph of the types of ateliers
drawings.notes: The nodes as on the page, with their formulas as the transcription reads them: atelier général (circled A), atelier divisible (crossed by the stroke up to the general atelier), atelier spatial (circled Sigma), atelier local, atelier fidèle, atelier ponctuel Sigma = P(L), pencil "at. mod ?", (circled L) atelier ensembliste, atelier modéré, at. ens. modéré, maquette Sigma = P(A) in its pencil box, at. discret, at.-point; the strokes and arrows between them, dashed where dashed, the double arrow maquette - atelier modéré, and the orange horizontal line. Redrawn 2026-11-09 at 2 mm per unit with the labels at \small (the overlay of nodes and strokes was checked and kept); struck out and now omitted: the first "atelier modéré" at the top right and the struck word above at.-point (both were drawn grey before). The pencil NB box at the right edge and a few faint pencil strokes are left out. Still differs: the long curves are approximate, and the strokes stop near the labels rather than on them (the page joins words, not points). Redrawn 2026-11-09 (issue 128): to check again. 2026-11-13, Claude Opus 5.5, overlay check (issue 147): not compiled (no TeX in the session); the TikZ rasterised and laid over the 350 dpi colour render of the scan, with contrast-enhanced crops for the faint strokes. Nodes, labels and the straight strokes lie on the ink to within about 1 unit and were kept. Changed: the long curve from the circled A is two curves on the page, one to the struck first « atelier modéré » and one down to « atelier modéré » with its head (each now through points read on it); the heavy curve from the atelier fidèle carries its head at the top of the maquette and runs on into it; the thin pencil curve from the atelier fidèle to the atelier modéré is added (the second curve the transcription names); the strokes from the circled Sigma are read again: a thin solid pencil line to « atelier ponctuel », and the dashed line running down past the left of the ponctuel formula to « atelier ensembliste » (it was drawn ending at the formula); the pencil line to the atelier modéré starts right of the ponctuel formula (heavier at first) and is joined there by the dashed pencil stroke from « at. mod » with its second « ? »; the pencil box round the maquette moved up 1.3 units onto its ink; three short strokes added where they are (one down from « maquette », two dashes between « atelier ensembliste » and the maquette). Left out as before: the two struck words (crossings-out) and the pencil NB note at the right edge (a text box beside the graph, not part of it). Disagreement with the transcription, recorded in docs/review/transcription-readings-128-2026-11-12.md: the stroke from the atelier spatial to the atelier ponctuel is solid, and the dashed one goes to the atelier ensembliste.
drawings.disagreement: The transcription says the atelier ponctuel is joined to the atelier spatial by a dashed stroke; on the page that stroke is a thin solid pencil line, and the dashed line runs from the circled Sigma of the atelier spatial down to « atelier ensembliste ».

drawings.description: un graphe au crayon et à l'encre, de sommets S (en haut), LS, M (cerclés), SF, E, MF, EM (cerclé) et Mq (en bas) : S est relié à M par un arc épais et à LS ; SF est au centre, relié à S, à E et à MF ; M est relié à MF par un arc ; MF est relié à EM et à Mq ; LS est relié à E puis à EM. À côté : « DEQFLMPS » et dessous « Mq, Div, v, p ».
drawings.kind: graph on S, LS, M, SF, E, MF, EM, Mq
drawings.notes: Pencil and ink graph: S at the top joined to M by a thick arc and to LS; SF in the centre joined to S, E and MF; M joined to MF by an arc; MF to EM and Mq; LS to E, E to EM; LS, M and EM ringed. Beside it "DEQFLMPS" and under it "Mq, Div, v, p".

drawings.description: un graphe orienté, les flèches montant vers le haut (traits doublés à l'encre brune), avec hachures au crayon dans deux bandes. Au sommet G $(\mathcal{A})$. Au-dessous, à gauche S $(\Sigma$ ou $\mathcal{A})$ cerclé, au milieu F, à droite L ; sur l'arête de L à G un point « Div » ; sur l'arête de SF à S une marque « [S Div] ». Au niveau suivant SF, LS $(\Sigma$ ou $\mathcal{L})$ (cerclé) et FL $=$ P. Puis FLS $=$ E $(\mathcal{L})$ au centre et M (cerclé) à gauche. Puis Mq (sous M) et EM (cerclé, sous E). En bas D, recevant deux flèches venues de v et de p. Flèches : S, F, L $\to$ G ; SF $\to$ S et F ; LS $\to$ S et L ; P $\to$ F et L ; E $\to$ SF, LS, P ; M $\to$ SF ; Mq $\to$ M ; EM $\to$ M et E ; D $\to$ Mq et EM ; v, p $\to$ D. Pointillés de S à Div et de F à L.
drawings.notes: Oriented graph, arrows upwards (ink lines doubled in brown, drawn once): G (A) at the top; S (Sigma or A) ringed, F, L; Div on the edge L - G; [S Div] on the edge SF - S side; SF, LS (Sigma or L) ringed, FL = P; FLS = E (L) and M ringed; Mq and EM ringed; D, receiving the arrows from v and p. Arrows S, F, L -> G; SF -> S, F; LS -> S, L; P -> F, L; E -> SF, LS, P; M -> SF; Mq -> M; EM -> M, E; D -> Mq, EM; v, p -> D. The dotted strokes (S to Div, F to L side) are dashed here; the two hatched bands are pencil hatching. The notes in the left margin and below the graph are text and left out.

drawings.description: un triangle de sommets $a$ (en haut), $b$, $c$ ; la moitié gauche hachurée, un segment de $a$ au point $d$, marqué d'un gros point, sur le côté $[b,c]$.
drawings.notes: Triangle a (top), b, c; the left half hatched; a segment from a to the point d, marked by a big dot, on the side [b, c].

drawings.description: en haut à gauche, un treillis dessiné en perspective, comme un prisme hexagonal vu de biais : de $0$ partent des flèches vers $a$ (en passant par $a'$), $c$ et $b'$ ; de là vers $B$, $C$, $A$ (avec une étape marquée $A'$ entre $A$ et $1$), puis vers $1$ ; plusieurs flèches intérieures repassées et une étoile au centre. Au-dessous, un hexagone orienté de sommets $A$, $b$, $C$, $a$, $B$, $c$, les flèches allant des sommets bas $b$, $a$, $c$ vers les sommets $A$, $C$, $B$, doublé d'un arc de cercle.
drawings.kind: lattice in perspective and oriented hexagon
drawings.notes: Redrawn on tight crops with every vertex placed once and every arrow drawn between the same vertices (stopping just short of them, heads at the upper end). Top: the lattice of a cube seen obliquely: from 0 arrows to a (through a', which labels the edge), c and b'; a -> B, a -> C, c -> B, c -> A, b' -> C, b' -> A; then B -> 1, C -> 1 and A -> A' -> 1; the star in the centre. Corrected from the earlier redraw: the edge C -> 1 is the long vertical stroke on the page (it was drawn as a slanted arrow from the label C), and C is placed where the arrows from a and b' meet; his retraced strokes are drawn once. Bottom: the oriented hexagon A, b, C, a, B, c, its six edges oriented from b, a, c to A, C, B, doubled at the right and at the left by pencil arcs. A faint pencil square to the right of the lattice is not part of the mark and is left out. Still a reading: the exact place of C and of the star among the retraced inner strokes. Redrawn 2026-11-09 (issue 128): to check again. Question settled by a machine pass on the facsimile, 2026-11-12 (maths): in the lattice of the cube (0, then a, c, b', then B, C, A, then 1) C receives the arrows from a and b' and sends one arrow to 1: the long vertical stroke up to 1 starts at the point where the arrows from a and b' meet, the letter C stands just left of that point, and no other stroke leaves it towards 1. C and C -> 1 are as drawn. Not checked by a reader. 2026-11-13, Claude Opus 5.5, overlay check (issue 147): not compiled (no TeX in the session); the TikZ rasterised and laid over the 350 dpi colour render of the scan, with contrast-enhanced and tight colour crops of the centre. The lattice's vertices and its thirteen arrows, and the hexagon's six arrows and right pencil arc, lie on the ink to within about 1 unit and were kept. Changed: the arrow from 0 to a now carries its second head at a' (where the page has it, mid-way); the head of c -> A is drawn where the page has it, at about (43, 98.4), with the short stroke on to A carrying the second head under A; the left pencil arc of the hexagon moved 1.5 units out onto its ink, and the short pencil arc under a and the stroke that runs up to C from below are added; the labels 0, a', 1, A' and the lower a moved onto their ink. The inner marks of the lattice, left out before, are drawn as they stand rather than read: a short heavy arrow pointing up from the crossing of a -> C and c -> B, two heavy marks shaped like the figure 4 (one on a -> C at about (43, 42), one on c -> A at about (59, 38): retraced heads, or the figure 4), a heavy mark with a dot and a small A right of the centre, and a short tick under C -> 1. Left out: the heavy scribble below the second of those marks (about (59-63, 40-45)), a crossing-out, and two specks inside the hexagon that may come from the typed text showing through.
